text:
maya: Heads up — after landing opt-kselect v2 + allocator-windowing we saw OOM spikes on a subset of G1 prod nodes during the 09:00 -> 10:00 deploy window. Posting quick notes and captures below.

alex: Are the OOMs tied to long sequences or to batch size/padding?

sam: Correlates with mixed-seq batches. Prefix-cache hit-rate dropped during the spike (0.72 -> 0.45) and eviction counts spiked ~3x.

jordan: Can you upload the nsys summary or flamegraph?

maya: Quick nsys snippet:
```
nsys summary: fused_attn_v2 workspace alloc spikes at seq>1024
avg workspace size: 48MB -> 112MB (for fused_attn_v2)
cudaMalloc spikes around kernel selection time
dynamic_batcher pads many small seqs up to the max in batch
```

li: Looks like the kernel selector now prefers fused_attn_v2 for seq>=512. For our mixed load that causes a ton of padding overhead (workspace scales with padded length). Suggest: prefer streaming/fallback kernel for mixed batches or raise fused threshold.

alex: Also seeing allocator fragmentation in logs — slab allocator reports several 8MB free fragments that are non-contiguous. The new windowing stategy increased churn.

sam: On the prefix cache side: TTL is currently 10m. With more concurrent requests and larger padded workspaces prefixes stayed referenced longer, preventing evictions and growing resident memory.

maya: Did a quick sim: reducing TTL 10m->3m lowered peak GPU resident by ~18% and only reduced logical hit-rate from 72% -> 68% on our trace. Shard sizing: moving to 128 shards from 64 flattened eviction spikes (less bursty per-shard high-water).

jordan: Another mitigation: emergency reserve pool. Keep a single reserved buffer (256MB) that allocator never hands out. On OOM attempt, drain reserve and retry slower paths. Minimal change but buys headroom.

li: Also we can reuse workspace buffers across kernels in the same request (attention -> ffn) to avoid multiple simultaneous workspace allocations. In local testing reuse cut transient workspace allocations nearly 50%.

alex: For batching heuristics: throttle dynamic_batcher when max_seq_in_batch > 512. Either split batch or limit aggregation to reduce padding blowup. Simpler than changing kernel defaults.

ci-bot: Perf alert created: #perf-alerts/1905001234 — baseline -> current: p50 +2ms, p99 +120ms, OOM count 37 in 1h.

maya: Proposed plan: 1) revert kselect threshold for fused_attn_v2 to previous (maya) 2) add emergency reserve pool (li) 3) change prefix TTL for prod-tier caches 10m->3m + increase shards to 128 (sam) 4) throttle dynamic_batcher for seq>512 (alex) 5) add workspace reuse path for in-request kernels (li). I'll open PRs.

alex: I'll own rolling canary + dashboards for the changes. Will add histogram of padded_length and per-kernel workspace usage.

sam: I'll run TTL/shard sims and post hit-rate vs memory curves.

jordan: I'll spin up a tiny repro harness that generates mixed small/large seq batches to reproduce deterministically.

maya: Thanks everyone — I'll post PR links and traces later today. :thumbsup:
